newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel barges bit firmer, gain may buoy cargoes.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel barges bit firmer, gain may buoy cargoes.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges were steady to a bit firmer at the start of the week on Monday, cargoes were flat with prospects for gains soon and one percent was said to be overvalued with little buying interest.
After initially changing hands at $82.75 fob ARA, high sulphur fuel oil barges dipped to $82 before moving up to trade at $82.50/$83, compared with Friday's closing level of $82.50.
A small parcel was done at $83.50 fob but it was for Tuesday delivery and was not reflective of the market, traders said.
"The market is actually between $82 and $83 and may be actually closer to $82 now," one trader said in late afternoon.
Bunkers were done at $84.50, $85 and $86 delivered on board for 380 CST, while 180 CST was heard done at $91 in Rotterdam, a few dollars higher than late last week.
"(Barge) buyers are not very interested and bunker enquiries were not fabulous either," a trader said.
High sulphur cargoes were seen flat with two cargoes unsold, but traders said the market may draw strength from the little firmness in barges and steady prices for Russian material.
A Scandinavian refiner cut its offering price a few dollars for utility grade material to a floating high fob plus $1.50 or about $74 fob.
But Russian cracked M-100 bought by a refiner recently was heard re-offered at two means plus $2.50
A trader was heard still offering a large cracked cargo out of Bilbao and one trader said they may move it into the bunker market soon if it went unsold.
One percent was quietly talked, with one seller still offering at $94.50 fob and the a second seller at a floating price equivalent to $95, a price dismissed by many as expensive.
A bid was heard at $92, slightly less than Friday and at the same level as July swaps, but no deals were heard done.
"I think this market is holding up for lack of activity really. One player bid it up as it is pricing into Israel," one trader said. "I see it more like $91/$93 in reality".
